history.dynasty: Established 1680 CE by Acharya Ram Pandey (per local sources)
history.period: 1680 CE (CONFLICT: one travel review calls it a 16th-century temple - verify)
history.summary: Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Chandika, a fierce form of Durga/Parvati, on the hills across the Saryu river opposite Bagnath temple, about 1.5-2 km from Bageshwar town, near the Saryu-Gomti confluence. Legend says Chandika manifested here to vanquish the demon kings Shumbha and Nishumbha. Local sources (chardhamtours.in, sacredyatra.com) date the temple's establishment to 1680 by Acharya Ram Pandey, whose descendants remain its priests today; one travel review instead calls it a 16th-century temple - CONFLICT (verify). Thousands of devotees gather here each Navratri. The site offers panoramic views of Bageshwar town, the river confluence, and Bagnath temple.

name: Chandika Temple
town_description: Bageshwar is the headquarters town of Bageshwar district in Uttarakhand's Kumaon region, set at the confluence of the Saryu and Gomati rivers between the Bhileshwar and Nileshwar hills. Historically a trade mart between Tibet and Kumaon, it is a temple town known for Bagnath temple, the Gauri Udiyar cave, and the Chandika temple on the hillside.

travel.road: ~1.5-2 km from Bageshwar town; cross the Saryu river to the hill opposite Bagnath temple; a motorable road reaches the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to May (per chardhamtours.in); Navratri for the main festival crowds
